/guide/piano-chords.h1: How to Play Chords on Piano
/guide/piano-chords.scope: A guided first task, not the whole dictionary or a promise of a complete course.

content.heading: Start with one chord, not a whole song
paragraphs: Begin by finding C, E and G. These three different note names form the C major triad. A chord symbol is a compact instruction about a group of pitches; it does not by itself tell you the rhythm, register or best hand placement for a piece.

The reference below starts with four specific triads: C major, A minor, F major and G major. You do not need to learn every chord family before comparing these examples. Use the chart to look up another chord once this task is clear.
steps: Say C, E and G aloud.
Locate one example of those notes on a keyboard.
Read the chord symbol C, then check the C-major reference.

supplemental_blocks.evidence_status: [推断] original examples and pedagogy applying cited rules

content.heading: Read the root and quality separately
paragraphs: C names a major triad on C. Am names a minor triad on A. The letter supplies the root; the quality tells you which interval pattern is being used. A slash adds a bass instruction: Am/C uses A, C and E with C as the lowest sounding note.
In a formula such as 1–3–5, the numbers describe chord members measured from the root using the major-scale reference. In 1–♭3–5, the third is lowered a semitone. These are not finger numbers.

supplemental_blocks.evidence_status: [推断] original examples and pedagogy applying cited rules

content.heading: Choose a hand example with a stated scope
paragraphs: Each thumb is finger 1, each middle finger is 3 and each little finger is 5. The same numbers name the same digits on both hands, not permanent keyboard positions.

The Yamaha C-major illustration supports a right-hand root-position example using 1–3–5. The current C-major detail adds its own separately sourced left-hand example. Use those examples only for the stated voicing; do not copy them onto every inversion or transition.

A left-hand bass plus a right-hand chord is a separate arrangement task. The overall bass must be taken from both hands together. A right-hand shape alone does not determine the inversion of the combined sound.

supplemental_blocks.evidence_status: [推断] original examples and pedagogy applying cited rules

content.heading: Keep C and E: compare C with Am/C
paragraphs: Use C4–E4–G4, then C4–E4–A4, then return to C4–E4–G4. The two lower pitches stay fixed while the upper pitch changes. The middle chord is Am/C because C is the lowest note.

This is an original note-connection example, not an assigned fingering. There is no promise that a particular hand size should use the same fingers for both shapes. The task is to identify what changes, then try it at a manageable pace.
steps: Read the first three notes and name the chord.
Change G4 to A4, leaving C4 and E4 unchanged.
Name the bass of the middle chord: C4.
Answer: the middle chord is Am/C, not root-position Am.

supplemental_blocks.evidence_status: [推断] original examples and pedagogy applying cited rules

content.heading: Use the browser exercise for the right task
paragraphs: The existing chord builders check which pitch classes you selected. A correct result means the requested note set was selected; it does not mean your timing, hand position or acoustic playing has been assessed.

A useful sequence is to identify the notes here, try the object’s own builder, and then use the printed or on-screen reference beside your instrument. Keep those three activities distinct rather than treating a browser score as a performance grade.

supplemental_blocks.evidence_status: [推断] original examples and pedagogy applying cited rules

content.heading: Move from a chord to a short progression
paragraphs: After identifying C, Am, F and G individually, read C–G–Am–F as a sequence of chord names. In C major, its scale-degree pattern is I–V–vi–IV. A progression page can then specify the meter, duration and particular voicings.
The chord chart is for lookup. This guide is for learning how to use one result. The by-key page answers a different question: which triads can be built from the notes of one selected scale?

supplemental_blocks.evidence_status: [推断] original examples and pedagogy applying cited rules

content.heading: Questions and answers

rows: Do I always play chords with my right hand?
No. Which hand plays which notes depends on the arrangement. The reference presents separate examples, not a rule that chords belong to one hand.
Is Am/C the same as playing only C?
No. Am/C still contains A, C and E; the slash only specifies C in the bass.
Can I play all four starter chords with one fixed fingering?
This guide does not prescribe that. Use the hand-specific evidence for each stated voicing rather than extending one example to every shape.

/keyboard-notes/finger-numbers.h1: Piano Finger Numbers: Left and Right Hand
/keyboard-notes/finger-numbers.scope: Finger-number identification; not a universal fingering chart for every chord, scale or song.

content.heading: Both thumbs are 1
paragraphs: On each hand, 1 means thumb, 2 index finger, 3 middle finger, 4 ring finger and 5 little finger. The numbering does not continue from 5 on the left hand to 6 on the right. Each hand has its own 1–5 set.
LH means left hand; RH means right hand. Read the hand label before interpreting a number. LH 1 means left thumb, while RH 1 means right thumb.

supplemental_blocks.evidence_status: [推断] original examples and pedagogy applying cited rules

content.heading: Read the two hands from the player’s view
paragraphs: The planned diagram uses the view of a player looking down at the backs of both hands. With the left hand drawn on the left and the right hand on the right, the two thumbs sit toward the middle.

Across the left-hand diagram, the displayed finger labels run 5, 4, 3, 2, 1 from left to right. Across the right-hand diagram, they run 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. These are identification labels, not a prescribed posture or an anatomical teaching model.

supplemental_blocks.evidence_status: [推断] original examples and pedagogy applying cited rules

content.heading: A finger number is not a permanent key assignment
paragraphs: Finger 1 does not always play C. A fingering instruction chooses a digit for a note in a particular passage. A different register, neighboring notes or hand may call for a different choice.
A chord’s root and its lowest note are also not finger numbers. In an inversion, the chord member in the bass changes, while the numbering of your hands remains the same.

supplemental_blocks.evidence_status: [推断] original examples and pedagogy applying cited rules

content.heading: Keep three kinds of numbers apart
paragraphs: Finger 3 identifies the middle finger of the specified hand. Scale degree 3 identifies the third degree of a scale. The 4 in C4 identifies an octave register. None of these numbers can be substituted for another.
For example, E is the third degree of C major. That does not require every E to be played with finger 3. C4 remains the same pitch label whichever digit presses the key.

supplemental_blocks.evidence_status: [推断] original examples and pedagogy applying cited rules

content.heading: Try four reading checks
paragraphs: Cover the answers, interpret each instruction, then compare. These questions check labels rather than piano technique.
steps: C4 → the note C in octave 4, not finger 4.

supplemental_blocks.evidence_status: [推断] original examples and pedagogy applying cited rules

content.heading: Look up fingering for an exact example
paragraphs: After learning the labels, choose a page that states the chord or scale, hand, direction where relevant, and octave range. Read its source and limitation. A generic hand chart alone cannot supply all of those decisions.
Use the existing C-major chord page for a root-position example and the C-major scale page for its own stated scale pattern. Do not assume the chord’s 1–3–5 pattern is the scale’s complete fingering.

supplemental_blocks.evidence_status: [推断] original examples and pedagogy applying cited rules

content.heading: Questions and answers

rows: Is the left thumb number 5?
No. Both thumbs are 1. The left hand looks reversed on the page, but its numbering by finger identity does not change.
Does LH 3 mean the third key from the left?
No. It means the middle finger of the left hand. A separate note name or notation tells you which pitch to play.
Does this chart tell me how to finger any song?
No. It explains the numbers. A complete passage may require its own context-specific fingering.

/chords/by-key.scope: Seven prepared key tables, not every key and not all possible chromatic harmony.

content.heading: A key is not the same filter as a chord root
paragraphs: Choosing root C in the chord chart finds chords built on C, such as C major and C minor. Choosing the key of C major here lists triads built on each degree of the C major scale.
The prepared tables cover C, G, D, A, E and F major, plus D minor. They show a deliberately limited set of keys rather than a claim to every scale, mode or borrowed chord.

supplemental_blocks.evidence_status: [推断] original examples and pedagogy applying cited rules

content.heading: Read the degree before the symbol
paragraphs: A degree number locates a chord’s root within the selected scale. Uppercase Roman numerals mark major triads, lowercase ones mark minor triads, and a diminished marker identifies the diminished triad.
In a major key the diatonic triad pattern is I–ii–iii–IV–V–vi–vii°. The note spelling changes with the key, so copying only a row’s white-key shape is not a transposition method.

supplemental_blocks.evidence_status: [推断] original examples and pedagogy applying cited rules

content.heading: Read C major as a complete seven-row table
paragraphs: The C-major triads are C, Dm, Em, F, G, Am and B diminished. Their chord tones come from C, D, E, F, G, A and B. A row for B diminished belongs in this table even though the current major/minor detail template cannot render it as a full object page.
A table row may therefore be a complete written reference without having a dedicated detail link. Keep the row visible and only provide a link when the requested detail actually exists.

supplemental_blocks.evidence_status: [推断] original examples and pedagogy applying cited rules

content.heading: Keep D natural minor and its altered options separate
paragraphs: D natural minor uses D, E, F, G, A, B-flat and C. Its diatonic triads are Dm, E diminished, F, Gm, Am, B-flat and C.

Minor-key music can raise C to C-sharp. That change makes A major available as V and C-sharp diminished as a leading-tone triad. Show these as raised-leading-tone alternatives rather than replacing the natural-minor row without explanation.

supplemental_blocks.evidence_status: [推断] original examples and pedagogy applying cited rules

content.heading: Build a row instead of memorizing a shape
paragraphs: Take a scale degree as the root, then select the third and fifth scale notes above it, cycling through the same scale. Preserve each note’s spelling and compare the intervals to identify the quality.
For example, the chord on E in C major uses E–G–B, so it is minor. In E major, the chord on E uses E–G-sharp–B, so it is major. The letter E alone does not determine the quality.

supplemental_blocks.evidence_status: [推断] original examples and pedagogy applying cited rules

content.heading: Turn a table into a progression
paragraphs: Choose I–V–vi–IV in C major to obtain C–G–Am–F. Choosing the same degrees in A major gives A–E–F-sharp minor–D. These are applications of the same harmonic pattern, not the same pitches.
A key table tells you which chords belong to the stated scale collection. It does not identify a whole song’s key from a single chord or prohibit chords borrowed from elsewhere.

supplemental_blocks.evidence_status: [推断] original examples and pedagogy applying cited rules

content.heading: Questions and answers

rows: Are chords in C major all rooted on C?
No. The table includes triads rooted on all seven scale degrees. Root C and key C major are different queries.
Why is there a diminished row without a detail button?
The table’s written data can be supported before a dedicated diminished-chord interactive template exists. Missing a detail page is not a reason to omit the scale degree.
Can a minor key use a major V?
Yes. Raising the leading tone supplies a major dominant triad. The table labels that option separately from its natural-minor basis.

supplemental_blocks.evidence_status: [推断] scoped explanation; feature statements conditional on implementation

/chord-progressions.scope: Three patterns in three keys: nine original four-bar realizations; not an unrestricted progression generator.

content.heading: Start with one four-bar example
paragraphs: Read C–G–Am–F as four chord changes. The prepared example gives each chord one bar of 4/4, with four quarter-note beats per bar. Its pattern is I–V–vi–IV in C major.
The dataset contains three patterns in C, E and A major. Each version includes a specific register and note list. These are short teaching examples, not copied song arrangements.

supplemental_blocks.evidence_status: [推断] original examples and pedagogy applying cited rules

content.heading: Separate the pattern from its voicing
paragraphs: Roman numerals identify degrees relative to the selected key. They do not specify the octave, hand, inversion, rhythm or instrument sound. Those choices must be given by the individual realization.

Changing the key changes the pitches while retaining the degrees. Changing the voicing can retain the chord names while rearranging which notes are lowest. Neither operation should silently change an advertised example.

supplemental_blocks.evidence_status: [推断] original examples and pedagogy applying cited rules

content.heading: Compare three different endings
paragraphs: I–V–vi–IV ends this four-bar unit on IV, making it useful for observing what happens when the sequence repeats. I–vi–IV–V finishes on V, so a following I changes the sense of arrival. I–IV–V–I includes that return in its final bar.

These descriptions tell you where the prepared unit starts and ends. They do not guarantee a happy, sad or beautiful effect. Tempo, texture, register, surrounding music and the listener can change that impression.

supplemental_blocks.evidence_status: [推断] original examples and pedagogy applying cited rules

content.heading: Read first, then try the changes
paragraphs: Read one bar’s symbol and exact notes before moving to the next. When playback is implemented, the active bar, sounding pitches and displayed notes must use the same data. No sound should start merely because the page loads.

The current examples do not prescribe transition fingerings, a minimum practice speed or a fixed hand allocation. Work with the note references first rather than treating these arrays as a complete piano-performance lesson.
steps: Name one chord’s three tones without looking at its answer.
Compare the notes of two adjacent bars.
Try the change, then return to the first bar.

supplemental_blocks.evidence_status: [推断] original examples and pedagogy applying cited rules

content.heading: Low register changes the listening example
paragraphs: Several preserved examples begin in octave 3. These are intentional reference registers, not a recommendation that every left-hand accompaniment should use close-position low triads.
An alternative with wider spacing or a separate bass would need its own note data and explanation. Do not label the same MIDI array as a new left-hand or jazz voicing.

supplemental_blocks.evidence_status: [推断] original examples and pedagogy applying cited rules

content.heading: Use individual chord pages when a change is unclear
paragraphs: A progression should not hide uncertainty about an individual chord. Open that chord’s reference to check the third, bass or spelling, then return to the same bar of the sequence.
The reference tables remain readable without JavaScript. A transport, automatic looping or live performance feedback must not be advertised until those behaviors are actually implemented and tested.

supplemental_blocks.evidence_status: [推断] original examples and pedagogy applying cited rules

content.heading: Questions and answers

rows: How many progressions are included?
Three degree patterns, each realized in C, E and A major, for nine four-bar examples.
Does a major-key pattern always sound happy?
No. The pattern does not determine an emotional response on its own. Mood labels should not replace note, rhythm and context information.
Do the Roman numerals tell me which fingers to use?
No. They label harmonic degrees. Fingerings and hand allocation are separate decisions.

supplemental_blocks.evidence_status: [推断] scoped explanation; feature statements conditional on implementation

/chords/finder.scope: Requires a new bounded matching tool. B3’s pitch-class practice checker is not a general chord finder.

content.heading: Enter what you know, not a guessed chord name
paragraphs: Enter pitch names with octave numbers, such as C4, E4 and G4. Keep the original spelling visible. The matcher can compare sounding pitch classes, but the result should still explain its chosen note names.

With exact octaves, the lowest supplied pitch is known. An empty optional bass field does not erase that information. A separate pitch-class-only input mode may genuinely have an unknown bass and must be labeled differently.

supplemental_blocks.evidence_status: [推断] original examples and pedagogy applying cited rules

content.heading: Read candidates, bass and scope together
paragraphs: C4–E4–G4 supports C major. E3–G3–C4 has the same chord-tone set but places E in the bass, so C/E describes that input more precisely.

The tool needs to distinguish a chord’s root from its lowest note. It also needs a stated vocabulary: not finding a name in the supported set does not prove that the selected notes are musically invalid.

supplemental_blocks.evidence_status: [推断] original examples and pedagogy applying cited rules

content.heading: Some note sets have more than one useful name
paragraphs: The pitch classes C, E, G and A can be read as C6 or Am7. With the exact input C4–E4–G4–A4, the lowest note is C, so the alternate A-minor-seventh interpretation is Am7/C.
With A2–C4–E4–G4, A is lowest; Am7 and C6/A are candidate descriptions. Musical context can favor a reading, but the supplied notes alone do not establish a unique compositional intention.

supplemental_blocks.evidence_status: [推断] original examples and pedagogy applying cited rules

content.heading: Repeated roots change spacing, not the note set
paragraphs: C4–C5–E5–G5 contains two Cs in different octaves. Deduplicate pitch classes for matching while retaining the full pitch list for display and the bass calculation.
Do not discard octaves before identifying the lowest pitch. Otherwise the tool can produce a valid chord class with an incorrect slash-bass label.

supplemental_blocks.evidence_status: [推断] original examples and pedagogy applying cited rules

content.heading: Show an honest no-match state
paragraphs: C4–G4 lacks a third, so a major/minor-triad-only matcher cannot determine major versus minor. That is a scope limitation, not evidence that two notes cannot form a useful sonority.
For C4–C♯4–D4, report that no supported match was found. Do not force the nearest major chord, delete an inconvenient note or present an unverified AI-generated name as certain.

supplemental_blocks.evidence_status: [推断] original examples and pedagogy applying cited rules

content.heading: This input does not identify a song key or assess playing
paragraphs: A chord candidate is not a song-key result. A written-note input is also not microphone recognition, MIDI capture or a measurement of timing and technique.

The prepared example set includes sixth and seventh candidates as well as triads. Those types require their own matching vocabulary. They must not be passed to the current three-note B3 detail validator as though it already supports them.

supplemental_blocks.evidence_status: [推断] original examples and pedagogy applying cited rules

content.heading: Questions and answers

rows: Why are there multiple results?
Different chord interpretations can share a pitch-class set. The bass and musical context help explain the alternatives.
Does an empty bass field mean the bass is unknown?
Not when notes include octaves. The lowest entered pitch already supplies a bass; only genuinely register-free input lacks that information.
Does no match mean the notes are wrong?
No. It means no match was found within the tool’s advertised vocabulary and rules.
